value.title: The /pij community route and optional templates
value.summary: Roadmap 001 s10: the pij skill gets a token-lean community route that teaches the prime to set up and run an emergent community (PEC), the PM to assign and release seats for its work, and the PA to see memory written before compacts; plus the optional role templates as examples.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Delivers req-15, req-29 (C28, growing a PEC from need) and the rest of req-13 and req-27; builds c-skill and finishes c-templates. Depends on s03 (templates) and s09 (prompts). Wording is PEC (C26, C18): build what the work needs now, reshape as it changes; templates are examples. Workers are told what to do by their packets, not the route.

sections.name: goals
value: Roadmap 001 s10: the pij skill gets a token-lean community route that teaches the prime to set up and run an emergent community (PEC), the PM to assign and release seats for its work, and the PA to see memory written before compacts; plus the optional role templates as examples.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Anything another roadmap step owns; see roadmap 001.

value.claim: Route. `skills/pij/references/routes/community.md` (and its SKILL.md routing entry) teaches the prime (stand up and reshape a community from needs), the PM (assign and release for its work; claims via s11) and the PA (memory before compacts), linking the doc procedures; token-lean.

Optional templates. v1 templates for some or all of: devcontainer, researcher, note-taker, topic expert, docs-keeper, infra, release, test and QA, designer, transcriber; each validates, is public-safe, and is marked as an example.
Fresh-prime canary. A seat with no prior context follows only the route and stands up a directory with core roles and a security role in a scratch project; where it hesitated is fixed or recorded.
F23 (low, s03 dogfood): `pij directory templates --show <name>[@vN]` prints a template's body (and its embedded path), so a prime can read a template before `add --from template:`.
Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). Docs and embedded templates only: no launch, loop or timer.

Docs and states. In this PR: roadmap s10 goes to complete (plan cell docs/plans/204-community-route); req-13, req-15, req-27 and req-29 go to shipped (s09 adds the req-29 row); c-skill and c-templates go to shipped. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

Growing a PEC (ruling C28, req-29). The route teaches the prime and PMs to recommend roles from need and keep the fleet small but expert: the signals for a new role (the same system or paths across tasks, a finding re-derived, a judgment that must be independent of the author, a seat carrying two domains, a path needing one owner) and against (one-off work, overlap with an existing role, nothing worth remembering, mostly idle); a role is not a seat (many cold roles, few live seats); boundary reviews (split, merge, retire); every recommendation names its signal; templates stay examples. With C30, the route and the template README say why a PEC exists: lasting problem-space knowledge held by specialist roles in memory and outputs that outlive seats, not only for engineering; "worth remembering" is a signal for a role. The route stays within its 100-line budget; lungfish gives a docs-system verdict on the wording before the PR is marked ready.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Read first: skills/pij/SKILL.md routing, skills/pij/references/community/, templates/roles/ (s03), plan 191's canary approach. Canary harness: OMP by default (AGENTS.md); OMP refuses linked worktrees, so use a plain clone as plan 191 did.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
